Triggers.value: People who look similar to the victims
When people say things like my ex

Maladaptive Strategies.value: I think about how life would have been different if the event had not occurred
become overly compliant when feeling threatened

Threat.value: Suddenly feeling or acting as if the stressful experience were actually happening again
Sudden movements by others put me immediately on guard
I feel unsafe unless my back is against a wall where I can see the room

Memory.value: I can't seem to put the frightening event into words.
When I remember the event I feel intense guilt
Remembering the event brings back the same terror I felt at the time

vignette: Rukmini's life had been a carefully constructed balance of family, business, and community. As the owner of a bustling convenience store in a predominantly South Asian neighborhood, she was well-known for her warm smile and quick wit. But it all began to unravel on a fateful evening three years ago, when a man she knew from the community assaulted her in the back room of her store. The details of that night still lingered, refusing to be put into words. Rukmini's mind would freeze, unable to articulate the sequence of events or the emotions that had coursed through her body. All she could recall was the feeling of being trapped, with no escape from the attacker's grasp. The guilt and terror that followed were suffocating, making it impossible for her to shake off the sense of responsibility she felt for not fighting back. As time passed, Rukmini began to notice subtle changes in her daily routine. She started avoiding public transportation, opting instead to drive or take taxis, even for short distances. The thought of being packed into a crowded bus or train, surrounded by strangers, made her skin crawl. She couldn't explain why, but the feeling of vulnerability was overwhelming. Conversations with friends and family became increasingly strained, as Rukmini found herself wincing at certain names or phrases that brought back memories of the assault. Her husband would sometimes mention his ex-girlfriend in passing, unaware of the emotional turmoil it sparked within her. She'd force a smile and change the subject, but the internal monologue would begin: "If only I had been more careful...if only I had fought back..." Rukmini's shop became her sanctuary, but even there, she felt trapped. Sudden movements by customers or employees would put her immediately on guard, as if ready to defend herself from an unseen threat. She'd position herself near the counter, with her back against the wall, scanning the room for potential dangers. The flashbacks were the worst - moments when time seemed to warp and she was reliving the assault all over again. Her heart racing, her vision blurring, Rukmini would be transported back to that fateful night, powerless to stop it. The world around her would fade away, replaced by the sounds, smells, and sensations of the attack. As the months went by, Rukmini's relationships began to suffer. She became increasingly withdrawn, struggling to connect with loved ones or even engage in conversations about everyday topics. Her business started to falter as well, as she found it difficult to manage staff or interact with customers without feeling a sense of unease. One day, while arranging stock on the shelves, Rukmini caught a glimpse of herself in the mirror - pale, thin, and haunted-looking. It was then that she realized she couldn't keep living like this. The thought of her daughter growing up without a happy, carefree mother was too much to bear. With a newfound determination, Rukmini began searching for help, hoping to break free from the grip of her memories and reclaim her life. As she sat in the therapist's office, fidgeting with her hands, Rukmini whispered: "I just want to be able to walk down the street without feeling like I'm going to die. I want to be me again - strong, confident, and free." The terror still lingered, but for the first time in years, she felt a glimmer of hope that things could change.
